content.user_title: Inspect Audio and Video with Mediabunny
content.value_statement: Reading media metadata consistently across web and server environments can require unfamiliar APIs. This skill provides focused Mediabunny patterns for durations and video dimensions.
actual_capabilities: Provides a Mediabunny helper pattern for computing audio duration in seconds.
Provides a Mediabunny helper pattern for computing video duration in seconds.
Shows how to read display width and height from the primary video track.
Adapts Remotion public assets through the staticFile helper.
Explains when to use UrlSource or FileSource across supported environments.
limitations: Provides instructions and examples but does not inspect media files itself.
Covers duration and video dimensions, not transcoding, editing, or rendering.
Example URL sources disable retries and do not include production network handling.
Local file examples require the caller to supply a compatible File object.

use_cases.title: Match Composition Timing
use_cases.description: Read source footage duration before setting a Remotion composition length.

use_cases.title: Validate Uploaded Media
use_cases.description: Check browser-selected video dimensions before accepting an upload or selecting a layout.

use_cases.title: Catalog Media Metadata
use_cases.description: Extract durations from local audio and video files in a Node.js or Bun workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Read Audio Duration
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to get the duration of an audio URL with Mediabunny in TypeScript.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a focused audio metadata helper.

prompt_templates.title: Read Video Dimensions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mediabunny helper that returns a video URL's display width and height. Include handling for a missing video track.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs dimensions before laying out a video.

prompt_templates.title: Use Remotion Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the video duration helper for a file in Remotion's public directory using staticFile.
prompt_templates.scenario: A Remotion project needs metadata from a bundled asset.

prompt_templates.title: Support URL and Local Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Design reusable TypeScript utilities for audio duration, video duration, and dimensions. Explain UrlSource and FileSource choices for browsers, Node.js, and Bun.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced project supports several media sources and runtimes.

output_examples.input: Find the duration of an audio file from a public URL.
output_examples.output: A typed asynchronous helper creates a Mediabunny URL source, computes the duration, and returns the result in seconds.

output_examples.input: Check a local video's dimensions before rendering.
output: Use a file source for the supplied local file.
Return its display width and display height.

output_examples.input: Inspect a video stored in Remotion's public directory.
output_examples.output: Resolve the asset with staticFile, pass the resolved path to the helper, and use the returned duration for composition timing.

best_practices: Use staticFile for assets stored in a Remotion public directory.
Check that a primary video track exists before reading its dimensions.
Choose UrlSource for URLs and FileSource for caller-provided local files.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every media input contains a video track.
Do not treat instructional retry settings as complete production network policy.
Do not use these metadata helpers as a substitute for media validation or transcoding.

faq.question: Which metadata can this skill help retrieve?
faq.answer: It covers audio duration, video duration, and primary video display dimensions.

faq.question: Does it work with Remotion public assets?
faq.answer: Yes. Resolve the asset path with staticFile before passing it to the helper.

faq.question: Can I inspect a remote media URL?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use Mediabunny UrlSource for remote or browser-resolvable sources.

faq.question: Can I inspect local files?
faq.answer: Yes. Use FileSource with a compatible File object in the relevant browser, Node.js, or Bun workflow.

faq.question: Does this skill render or edit media?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on reading duration and dimension metadata.

faq.question: How does it handle videos without a video track?
faq.answer: The dimensions pattern checks for a primary video track and raises an error when none exists.
